findings: The methyl orange product is labelled 'p-dimethylaminoazo benzene' (the name of butter yellow) and drawn with N triple bond N; the redrawn figure names it methyl orange with -N=N-.

The book calls the phenylamine nitrogen sp3 hybridised while also describing its lone pair as delocalised. The Quick Check questions are given in English as printed, without answers; the Roman Urdu answers were derived for the lesson and need the second-person review.
The book's p125 scheme warms phenyldiazonium chloride with water (phenol + N2 + HCl) while Chapter 22 (p95) uses NaOH; the figure follows p125 and the Roman Urdu note explains the difference.

The methyl orange equation on p126 prints the azo link as N triple bond N and names the product p-dimethylaminoazo benzene (the butter-yellow name), and the coupling mechanism ends with '-H'; the redrawn figures show N=N, 'methyl orange' and -H+.
